assumptions: Static buffer management: capacity is evenly partitioned across VCs. Dynamic (linked-list / packet-table) management is not modelled and costs substantially more control logic.
VC slice depth is assumed a power of two, so index wraparound is free and the RAM address is a pure concatenation of {vc_id, index}. Non-power-of-two slices would require a modulo comparator per VC.
Route-computation results and assigned output VC are allocator state, not buffer state, and are excluded here to avoid double-counting against DSENT's existing allocator models.
The input-side credit proxy is not modelled. It is a timing optimisation (a local copy of the output-side credit count) and would add ceil(log2(depth)) flops per input VC.

Router.cc's own top-level ClockTree's area is excluded from its own SitePitch (one-pass), slightly underestimating wire length. This no longer applies to DFFRAM's row-enable path (Phase 4.1 replaced its BroadcastHTree with a plain buffer chain that has no SitePitch/wire term at all -- see the next assumption).
Cell areas remain DSENT's analytic values, which are 25-50% below measured ASAP7 cells (DFF -25%, NAND2/NOR2 -50%, INV -33%). This is largely common-mode in a ratio but not in an absolute number.
Credit round-trip latency is not modelled. A VC shallower than the round-trip will credit-stall; that is a throughput cost visible only in simulation, never in a static power or area figure.

Closure Task Part B: DFFRAM's own inter-cell interconnect is entirely unmodelled (README bug #4). Every net created via createNet() inside DFFRAM.cc (CKGate0_Out, EnBufOut_*, NAND2_CKGate1_Outs*, CKGate1_Outs*, RowBufOut_*, Dec_Out*, DFF_Out*, Mux_Out) is a bare ElectricalNet with zero distributed cap/res -- only CellMacros.cc's intra-CELL M1 stub (:322-327, load-independent, baked into each cell's own cached self-capacitance) is modelled; nothing models the wire BETWEEN cells. Estimated magnitude (DSENT's own calculateWireCapacitance on the Local layer, Bulk22LVT.model, same formula the codebase already uses for BroadcastHTree/RepeatedLink, just not applied here): a single minimum-size gate input (NAND2/INV/BUF X1, A_Cap) is ~4.526e-16 F. One local-layer, one-gate-pitch (120nm) hop is ~2.049e-17 F, ~4.5% of that gate load; a more realistic several-cell hop (480nm, 4 gate pitches) is ~8.195e-17 F, ~18% of that gate load -- both small and plausibly negligible for genuinely LOCAL point-to-point nets (the RowBuf chain, INV_CKGate1_i->DFF.CK). The ROW-ENABLE FANOUT net is a different story: it must physically span the full DFFRAM array (SitePitch = sqrt(array_area), which the old BroadcastHTree WAS sized against and the new EnBuf chain is NOT), hundreds of um at large N/B (e.g. ~495um at N=512,B=256) -- a Local-layer estimate over that distance would be ~100x+ a single gate's input cap, i.e. NOT negligible, though a real layout would use a higher (Intermediate/Global) metal layer for a span that large, not Local. Net effect: replacing the H-tree with a plain buffer chain (Phase 4.1) correctly fixed a topology mismatch (NumberLevels tied to log2(N) rather than to real electrical fanout) but also removed the ONLY wire term the row-enable net had -- for large N/B this net is now modelled as having literally zero physical distance, which is itself an underestimate, just a much smaller and more defensible one than the 9-level H-tree it replaced. Not fixed here (no new modelling, per instructions) -- reported as a disclosed limitation.

Final Task: the write/clock-enable path fixes (Phase 4.1-4.3) made t_write_clock_path 3-10% of a 1ns period at every swept point. The READ path is now t_critical's binding term at EVERY (depth, width) point in this sweep -- it was previously masked at small N by the (now-fixed) write path being even slower. Two read-path components: t_read_access (CK->DFF internal CK-to-Q->Mux data path->Out) and t_read_addr_path (RDAddr->Mux select distribution->Mux data path-> Out); t_critical is the max of both, plus t_write_data_setup/t_write_clock_path. Multiplexer.cc's select-bit distribution had the SAME untapered-fanout defect the enable/row-clock chains had: exactly 2 fixed-size INVs per select bit at the top level, broadcasting unbuffered (plain net-to-net passthrough, zero buffering) through every recursion level below, to as many as NumberInputs/2 leaf MUX2 S0 pins for the LSB (measured directly: at N=512 this single under-sized inverter's own RC delay was 2.364e-10s of a 3.489e-10s total t_read_addr_path, 67.8%). Fixed the same way as the enable/row chains: each select bit now gets its own tapered BUF chain (Multiplexer.cc's SelectBufferStages/SelectBufferTaper parameters), sized from that bit's own real fanout (countSelectBitFanout(), a pure structural recursion mirroring the tree's own recursive construction) -- cut t_read_addr_path at N=512 from 3.489e-10s to 1.487e-10s (57.4%). The MUX TREE'S OWN DATA PATH (In->MUX2 chain-> Out) does NOT have this defect: every stage there has fanout exactly 1 (drives only the next level's single MUX2 input), so uniform minimum sizing is structurally correct, not a bug -- left unchanged. After this fix, e_read is NO LONGER expected to match earlier sessions' 'e_read must be unchanged' checks -- those checks were specifically about the DFFRAM clock/enable path never touching the read path, which was true until this fix touched Multiplexer.cc itself (part of the read datapath); e_read now correctly varies with the select-buffer chains' own N-dependent sizing, which is a correction (the old fixed-2-INV scheme charged the same select-buffer energy regardless of N, an inaccuracy), not a new defect. The remaining read-path depth scaling (t_read_addr_path/t_read_access both still grow with N) is a genuine structural property of an N:1 mux tree (ceil(log2(N)) series MUX2 delay stages) and was NOT further reduced -- there is no analogous untapered-fanout defect left to fix in it.
